selectionAndOwnershipAnalysis.groupInventory: PGID/PID only. DarwinActivity.group selects matching PGID and attempts every listed PID.
selectionAndOwnershipAnalysis.measuredMembership: Successful full records are checked for PID, birth, valid BSD state, current effective UID and requested PGID.
selectionAndOwnershipAnalysis.deniedMembership: On task-info EPERM/EACCES, read returns before BSD identity/UID/PGID checks. The denied member is therefore unknown rather than confirmed owned or confirmed unrelated.
selectionAndOwnershipAnalysis.registryCoverage: MacProcesses.pids filters current-effective-UID candidates, then OwnedNative recognizes executable/profile/argument/birth identities. Its set differs from the PGID inventory.
selectionAndOwnershipAnalysis.unrelatedProcessHypothesis: No evidence currently proves an unrelated process was included. A dedicated suite session and explicit descendant spawns make an inherited harness utility a concrete candidate. Snapshot staleness/PID reuse cannot be excluded without identity data.
selectionAndOwnershipAnalysis.importantDistinction: A helper launched by the harness is part of its subprocess graph even if a setuid exec changes its effective owner. Calling it unrelated solely because libproc denies counters would be unsupported.

psCandidate.staticEvidence: The pinned harness starts /bin/ps inside the suite PGID. The official Apple adv_cmds install script at the recorded commit installs ps outputs as root:wheel mode 4755.
psCandidate.conclusion: A setuid or protected ps descendant can explain the permission class in principle. It is not a proven attribution for this run.
psCandidate.otherPossibleCandidates: open, another native harness utility, or a changing/stale PID remain possible until actual identity evidence discriminates them.

whyNoSelectionOrSessionMoveYet: Filtering out EPERM members on presumed role or owner would turn an unknown resource/ownership interval into an accepted interval without evidence.
Moving a helper into a separate session would remove it from suite group accounting/cleanup unless a separately reviewed bounded accounting and exact ownership lifecycle were added.
Changing only HostProcess._process_rows would not cover the separate ps calls in ShimMonitor._run.
Normal harness subprocesses inherit the suite group deliberately; the new group itself does not prove every later member remains measurable under the original UID.
No observed denied PID role, UID or birth exists to validate the proposed target of a launch/selection change.
diagnosticOnlyCandidateRequirements: Retain original flavor-2 bytes/expectedBytes/errno and primary permission status before doing any supplementary read.
A supplementary full BSD-info query uses only the existing normal API. It must require exact response length, requested PID, valid birth time and valid state before trusting identity metadata.

Publish only allowlisted relation/status booleans and opaque tags, such as same/different/unknown UID or PGID, plus per-query numeric return/errno. Keep raw argv, tokens, paths and identity values private.
A later BSD snapshot describes that query time. Without a prior/expected birth match it cannot retrospectively identify the generation denied by flavor 2.
Always retain status unavailable on the permission branch. Do not synthesize measured/gone, zero RSS/CPU, an accepted resource sample or a cleanup authorization from the diagnostic read.
Full BSD flavor 3 is also CHECK_SAME_USER in the reference XNU implementation. A genuine different-UID ps can deny both flavor 2 and flavor 3; complete diagnostics are not guaranteed.

Where already permitted, inventory UID/PPID/PGID or standard short BSD metadata can be separate diagnostic evidence. Short BSD lacks the full birth tuple and must not replace complete generation validation.
A supplementary query failure must not replace the original permission failure or suppress its first-failure evidence.
No entitlement, signing, permission, user identity or resource-limit change is justified by this diagnosis.
portableTestsToReviewBeforeAnyFutureMacP: Task EPERM plus valid BSD identity still returns unavailable and null group totals.
Task EPERM plus BSD EPERM keeps both query details and the original reason.
Short, oversized, wrong-PID, invalid-birth and invalid-state BSD responses cannot create trusted identity metadata.
Different UID/PGID and expected-generation mismatch are diagnostic-only on this branch.
Per-query errno is preserved independently; supplementary exceptions do not overwrite task EPERM.
Serialization contains only permitted relation flags/tags and no raw identity or command data.
Mocked group_alive PermissionError and child reap ordering keep first failure, incomplete cleanup and unknown group state distinct.
